Now checking what's missing or flattened:

**Finding 1:** "her old hull's complexion was darkened like a French grenadier's, who has alike fought in Egypt and Siberia" — this is a distinctively Melvillean simile, stylistically signature. The draft says "long-seasoned, weather-stained" — the simile is gone.

**Finding 2:** "her masts stood stiffly up like the spines of the three old kings of Cologne" — draft says "her masts stood stiff" — the Cologne kings simile entirely gone.

**Finding 3:** "ancient decks were worn and wrinkled, like the pilgrim-worshipped flag-stone in Canterbury Cathedral where Becket bled" — draft says "decks worn like a pilgrim-worshipped flagstone" — the Canterbury/Becket specificity is erased. The phrase "where Becket bled" is the signature element; it's dropped.

**Finding 4:** "She was apparelled like any barbaric Ethiopian emperor, his neck heavy with pendants of polished ivory. She was a thing of trophies. A cannibal of a craft, tricking herself forth in the chased bones of her enemies." — "She was a thing of trophies" is absent in the draft.

**Finding 5:** The wigwam/wigwam description including "Pottowottamie Sachem's head" — the draft reduces this to one sentence "Aft of the mainmast stood a tent—wigwam-like—conical slabs of right-whale bone laced and tufted at the apex." The Pottowottamie Sachem simile and the triangular opening detail are gone.

**Finding 6:** Peleg's eye-wrinkles paragraph — "a fine and almost microscopic net-work of the minutest wrinkles interlacing round his eyes, which must have arisen from his continual sailings in many hard gales, and always looking to windward" — this is characteristic Melville physiognomy-reading prose. The draft says only "his eyes pursed by windward scowls."

**Finding 7:** "a bitter, hard task-master... when he sailed the old Categut whaleman, his crew, upon arriving home, were mostly all carried ashore to the hospital, sore exhausted and worn out." — the Categut story is absent.

**Finding 8:** Bildad's physical description scene — "bolt-upright, sat old Bildad, who always sat so, and never leaned, and this to save his coat tails" — the "to save his coat tails" detail is absent. Also "Bildad," cried Captain Peleg, "at it again, Bildad, eh? Ye have been studying those Scriptures, now, for the last thirty years..." — this comic exchange is absent.

**Finding 9:** "Be forewarned; Ahab's above the common; Ahab's been in colleges, as well as 'mong the cannibals" — partially present, but "Mark ye, be forewarned" is gone. Minor.

**Assessing severity:**

- The three Pequod similes (grenadier/Egypt-Siberia, kings of Cologne, Becket bled) are each distinctively shaped, critically noted, and stylistically signature. The Cologne simile is fully absent; the Becket simile is flattened (losing "where Becket bled"); the grenadier simile is fully absent. These are medium-to-high.
- The "three old kings of Cologne" simile is absent entirely — this is one of the most discussed details of the Pequod description. High.
- "where Becket bled" — flattened. Medium-high.
- Grenadier/Egypt-Siberia — absent. Medium.
- Pottowottamie Sachem — absent. Medium.
- Categut story — absent. Low-medium.
- "never leaned, and this to save his coat tails" / thirty-years Scripture exchange — absent. Medium.

The "three old kings of Cologne" is genuinely a textual-distinctiveness signature and is entirely absent. I'll rate it high.
